entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13031"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 2</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Zech.2.1-Zech.2.13">Zec 2:1-13</reference>. Third Vision. The man with the measuring-line.</title> <div sID="gen24463" type="x-p"/> The city shall be fully restored and enlarged (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.2-Zech.2.5">Zec 2:2-5</reference>). Recall of the exiles (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.6">Zec 2:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.7">7</reference>). Jehovah will protect His people and make their foes a spoil unto them (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.8">Zec 2:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.9">9</reference>). The nations shall be converted to Jehovah, as the result of His dwelling manifestly amidst His people (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.10-Zech.2.13">Zec 2:10-13</reference>).<div eID="gen24463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24464" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13031"/><hi type="bold">1. man with a measuring-line--</hi>the same image to represent the same future fact as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.40.3">Eze 40:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.4">47:4</reference>. The "man" is Messiah (see on <reference osisRef="Zech.1.8">Zec 1:8</reference>), who, by measuring Jerusalem, is denoted as the Author of its coming restoration. Thus the Jews are encouraged in Zechariah's time to proceed with the building. Still more so shall they be hereby encouraged in the future restoration. <div eID="gen24464" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 2 Zec 2:1-13 . Third Vision. The man with the measuring-line. The city shall be fully restored and enlarged ( Zec 2:2-5 ). Recall of the exiles ( Zec 2:6 , 7 ). Jehovah will protect His people and make their foes a spoil unto them ( Zec 2:8 , 9 ). The nations shall be converted to Jehovah, as the result of His dwelling manifestly amidst His people ( Zec 2:10-13 ). 1. man with a measuring-line-- the same image to represent the same future fact as in Eze 40:3 ; 47:4 . The "man" is Messiah (see on Zec 1:8 ), who, by measuring Jerusalem, is denoted as the Author of its coming restoration. Thus the Jews are encouraged in Zechariah's time to proceed with the building. Still more so shall they be hereby encouraged in the future restoration.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13034"/><div sID="gen24470" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13034"/><hi type="bold">4. this young man--</hi>So Zechariah is called as being still a youth when prophetically inspired [Grotius]. Or, he is so called in respect to his ministry or service (compare <reference osisRef="Num.11.27">Nu 11:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.1.1">Jos 1:1</reference>) [Vatablus]. Naturally the "angel that talked with" Zechariah is desired to "speak to" him the further communications to be made from the Divine Being.<div eID="gen24470" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24471" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">towns without walls for the multitude ... Cattle--</hi>So many shall be its inhabitants that all could not be contained within the walls, but shall spread out in the open country around (<reference osisRef="Esth.9.19">Es 9:19</reference>); and so secure shall they be as not to need to shelter themselves and their cattle behind walls. So hereafter Judea is to be "the land of unwalled villages" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.11">Eze 38:11</reference>). Spiritually, now the Church has extended herself beyond the walls (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.14">Ep 2:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.15">15</reference>) of Mosaic ordinances and has spread from cities to country villages, whose inhabitants gave their Latin name (pagani) to pagans, as being the last in parting with heathenism. <div eID="gen24471" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13035"/><div sID="gen24472" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13035"/><hi type="bold">5. I ... wall of fire round--</hi>Compare <reference osisRef="Zech.2.4">Zec 2:4</reference>. Yet as a city needs some wall, I Jehovah will act as one of fire which none durst approach (<reference osisRef="Zech.9.8">Zec 9:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.26.1">Is 26:1</reference>).<div eID="gen24472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24473" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">glory in the midst--</hi>not only a defense from foes outside, but a glory within (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.19">Is 60:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.23">Re 21:23</reference>). The same combination of "glory and defense" is found in <reference osisRef="Isa.4.5">Is 4:5</reference>, alluding to the pillar of cloud and fire which defended and enlightened Israel in the desert. Compare Elisha in Dothan (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.6.17">2Ki 6:17</reference>). As God is to be her "glory," so she shall be His "glory" (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.3">Is 62:3</reference>). <div eID="gen24473" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13036"/><div sID="gen24474" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13036"/><hi type="bold">6. flee from the land of the north--</hi>that is, from Babylon: a type of the various Gentile lands, from which the Jews are to be recalled hereafter; hence "the four winds of heaven" are specified, implying that they are to return from all quarters (<reference osisRef="Deut.28.64">De 28:64</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.16.15">Jr 16:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.17.21">Eze 17:21</reference>). The reason why they should flee from Babylon is: (1) because of the blessings promised to God's people in their own land; (2) because of the evils about to fall on their foe (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.7-Zech.2.9">Zec 2:7-9</reference>). Babylon was soon to fall before Darius, and its inhabitants to endure fearful calamities (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.20">Is 48:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.50.8">Jr 50:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.6">51:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.51.45">45</reference>). Many of the Jews in Zechariah's time had not yet returned to Judea. Their tardiness was owing to (1) unbelief; (2) their land had long lain waste, and was surrounded with bitter foes; (3) they regarded suspiciously the liberty of return given by Cyrus and Darius, as if these monarchs designed suddenly to crush them; (4) their long stay in Babylon had obliterated the remembrance of their own land; (5) the wealth and security there contrasted with Judea, where their temple and city were in ruins. All this betrayed foul ingratitude and disregard of God's extraordinary favor, which is infinitely to be preferred to all the wealth of the world [Calvin and Pembellus].<div eID="gen24474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24475" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for I have spread you abroad--</hi>The reasoning is: I who scattered you from your land to all quarters, can also gather you again to it. <div eID="gen24475" type="x-p"/>

The reason why they should flee from Babylon is: (1) because of the blessings promised to God's people in their own land; (2) because of the evils about to fall on their foe ( Zec 2:7-9 ). All this betrayed foul ingratitude and disregard of God's extraordinary favor, which is infinitely to be preferred to all the wealth of the world [Calvin and Pembellus]. for I have spread you abroad-- The reasoning is: I who scattered you from your land to all quarters, can also gather you again to it.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13037"/><div sID="gen24476" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13037"/><hi type="bold">7. O Zion ... daughter of Babylon--</hi>Thou whose only sure dwelling is "Zion," inseparably connected with the temple, art altogether out of thy place in "dwelling with the daughter of Babylon" (that is, Babylon and her people, <reference osisRef="Ps.137.8">Psa 137:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.1.8">Is 1:8</reference>).<div eID="gen24476" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24477" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">After the glory--</hi>After restoring the "glory" (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.5">Zec 2:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.4.5">Is 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.9.4">Ro 9:4</reference>) of Jehovah's presence to Jerusalem, He (God the Father) hath commissioned ME (God the Son, <reference osisRef="Isa.48.16">Is 48:16</reference>, the Divine Angel: God thus being at once the Sender and the Sent) to visit in wrath "the nations which spoiled you." Messiah's twofold office from the Father is: (1) to glorify His Church; (2) to punish its foes (<reference osisRef="2Thess.1.7-2Thess.1.10">2Th 1:7-10</reference>). Both offices manifest His glory (<reference osisRef="Prov.16.4">Pr 16:4</reference>).<div eID="gen24477" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24478" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">toucheth ... the apple of his eye--</hi>namely, of Jehovah's eye (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.10">De 32:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.17.8">Psa 17:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.7.2">Pr 7:2</reference>). The pupil, or aperture, through which rays pass to the retina, is the tenderest part of the eye; the member which we most sedulously guard from hurt as being the dearest of our members; the one which feels most acutely the slightest injury, and the loss of which is irreparable. <div eID="gen24478" type="x-p"/>

As the Jews' state between the return from Babylon and Christ's coming was checkered with much adversity, this prophecy can only have its fulfilment under Christ.<div eID="gen24480" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24481" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sent me--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.48.16">Is 48:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.61.1">61:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.10.36">Joh 10:36</reference>). <div eID="gen24481" type="x-p"/>

I will dwell in ... midst of thee--</hi>primarily at Messiah's first advent (<reference osisRef="Ps.40.7">Psa 40:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.14">Joh 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.2.9">Col 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Tim.3.16">1Ti 3:16</reference>); more fully at His second advent (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.10">Is 40:10</reference>). So <reference osisRef="Zech.9.9">Zec 9:9</reference>, where see on <reference osisRef="Zech.9.9">Zec 9:9</reference> (<reference osisRef="Isa.12.6">Is 12:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.27">Eze 37:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.14">Zep 3:14</reference>). Meanwhile God dwells spiritually in His people (<reference osisRef="2Cor.6.16">2Co 6:16</reference>). <div eID="gen24482" type="x-p"/>

So Zec 9:9 , where see on Zec 9:9 ( Is 12:6 ; Eze 37:27 ; Zep 3:14 ). Meanwhile God dwells spiritually in His people ( 2Co 6:16 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13040"/><div sID="gen24483" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13040"/><hi type="bold">11. many nations ... joined to the Lord in that day--</hi>The result of the Jews' exile in Babylon was that, at their subsequent return, through the diffusion of knowledge of their religion, many Gentiles became proselytes, worshipping in the court of the Gentiles (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.8.41">1Ki 8:41</reference>). Cyrus, Darius, Alexander, Ptolemy Philadelphus, Augustus, and Tiberius, paid respect to the temple by sending offerings [Grotius]. But all this is but a shadow of the future conversion of the Gentiles which shall result from Jehovah dwelling in Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Ps.102.15">Psa 102:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.102.16">16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.10">Php 2:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.11">11</reference>).<div eID="gen24483" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24484" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sent me unto thee--</hi>"unto thee" is here added to the same formula (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.9">Zec 2:9</reference>). Zion first shall "know (generally) that Jehovah of hosts hath sent" Messiah, by the judgments inflicted by Him on her foes. Subsequently, she shall know experimentally the particular sending of Messiah unto her. Jehovah here says, "I will dwell," and then that Jehovah of hosts sent Him; therefore Jehovah the Sender and Jehovah the Sent must be One. <div eID="gen24484" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 11. many nations ... joined to the Lord in that day-- The result of the Jews' exile in Babylon was that, at their subsequent return, through the diffusion of knowledge of their religion, many Gentiles became proselytes, worshipping in the court of the Gentiles ( 1Ki 8:41 ). Cyrus, Darius, Alexander, Ptolemy Philadelphus, Augustus, and Tiberius, paid respect to the temple by sending offerings [Grotius]. But all this is but a shadow of the future conversion of the Gentiles which shall result from Jehovah dwelling in Jerusalem ( Psa 102:15 , 16 ; Php 2:10 , 11 ). sent me unto thee-- "unto thee" is here added to the same formula ( Zec 2:9 ). Zion first shall "know (generally) that Jehovah of hosts hath sent" Messiah, by the judgments inflicted by Him on her foes. Subsequently, she shall know experimentally the particular sending of Messiah unto her. Jehovah here says, "I will dwell," and then that Jehovah of hosts sent Him; therefore Jehovah the Sender and Jehovah the Sent must be One.

Judah his portion in the holy land--</hi>Lest the joining of the Gentile "nations to Jehovah" (<reference osisRef="Zech.2.11">Zec 2:11</reference>) should lead the Jews to fear that their peculiar relation to Him (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.20">De 4:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.9.29">9:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.9">32:9</reference>) as "His inheritance" should cease, this verse is added to assure them of His making them so hereafter "again."<div eID="gen24485" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24486" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">choose Jerusalem again--</hi>The course of God's grace was interrupted for a time, but His covenant was not set aside (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.28">Ro 11:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.29">29</reference>); the election was once for all, and therefore shall hold good for ever. <div eID="gen24486" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13042"/><div sID="gen24487" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13042"/><hi type="bold">13. Be silent, O all flesh--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Hab.2.20">Ha 2:20</reference>). "Let all in silent awe and reverence await the Lord's coming interposition in behalf of His people!" The address is both to the Gentile foes, who prided themselves on their power as if irresistible, and to the unbelieving Jews, who distrusted God's promises as incredible. Three reasons why they must be silent are implied: (1) they are but "flesh," weak and ignorant; (2) He is Jehovah, all-wise and all-powerful; (3) He is already "raised up out of His place," and who can stand before Him? [Pembellus], (<reference osisRef="Ps.76.8">Psa 76:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.76.9">9</reference>).<div eID="gen24487" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24488" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he is raised up out of his holy habitation--</hi>that is, out of heaven (<reference osisRef="Deut.26.15">De 26:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.30.27">2Ch 30:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.63.15">Is 63:15</reference>), to judge and avenge His people (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.21">Is 26:21</reference>); or, "out of His holy" temple, contemptible and incomplete as it looked then when Zechariah urged them to rebuild it [Calvin]. But the call to all to "be silent" is rather when God has come forth from heaven where so long He has dwelt unseen, and is about to inflict vengeance on the foe, before taking up His dwelling in Zion and the temple. However, <reference osisRef="Ps.50.1">Psa 50:1</reference>, 2 ("Out of Zion"), <reference osisRef="Ps.50.3">Psa 50:3</reference> (compare <reference osisRef="Hab.2.3">Ha 2:3</reference>), <reference osisRef="Ps.50.4">Psa 50:4</reference>, favors Calvin's view. God is now "silent" while the Gentile foe speaks arrogance against His people; but "our God shall come and no longer keep silence"; then in turn must all flesh "be silent" before Him. <chapter eID="Zech.2"/>

navigation_sections.content_plain: Zec 2:1-13 . Third Vision. The man with the measuring-line. The city shall be fully restored and enlarged ( Zec 2:2-5 ). Recall of the exiles ( Zec 2:6 , 7 ). Jehovah will protect His people and make their foes a spoil unto them ( Zec 2:8 , 9 ). The nations shall be converted to Jehovah, as the result of His dwelling manifestly amidst His people ( Zec 2:10-13 ).
